context: Bivariate treemap encoding three variables: area=revenue, color=category, pattern shape=subcategory, pattern density=growth rate — an ambitious data visualization
first_impression: Colorful and information-dense with a deliberately chosen Tol bright palette and texture overlays, but the pattern density encoding for growth rate is barely perceptible at small cell sizes.
what_works: The Tol categorical palette (#4477AA, #EE6677, etc.) is a deliberate, publication-aware choice well above schemeCategory10 defaults; the three-section legend is clear and well-organized, correctly explaining all three encoding channels.
what_doesnt: The growth-rate-as-pattern-density encoding collapses into visual noise for the many small cells — the core bivariate idea fails at the rendered size where it matters most; category header labels in the top-padding area are only 11px and too faint to anchor sections reliably, leaving no strong typographic entry point into the chart.
